title: Fix centered spacing dimension calculation
description:
The _calculate_spaced_dimensions() function assumes uniform spacing, but centered spacing distributes spacing non-uniformly:
- Characters at center: tight spacing (target_spacing)
- Characters at edges: wide spacing (1.0)

This causes text to exceed calculated dimensions, resulting in clipping on right/bottom edges and blur clipping.

Fix required:
1. Update _calculate_spaced_dimensions() to accept center_spacing parameter
2. When center_spacing=True, calculate dimensions accounting for variable spacing per character
3. Use the interpolation formula: final_spacing = target + (1.0 - target) * normalized_distance
4. Ensure text stays within bounding box
5. Ensure blur padding extends far enough on all sides

This will prevent clipping of text and blur effects.
close_reason: Fixed dimension calculation for centered spacing - updated _calculate_spaced_dimensions() to accept center_spacing parameter and apply per-character interpolation. All 204 tests passing, visual validation confirms text and blur effects render without clipping.

title: Eliminate duplicate text rendering for typing effects
description:
When typing effects are enabled, _render_text_layer() calls render_text() twice per frame: once for full text, once for visible characters. This causes 2x font measurement overhead, 2x PIL drawing operations, and 2x image allocation per frame. 

For typing effects, render once and crop/clip to visible characters, or cache measurement and only re-render visible portion. This significantly impacts frame generation performance.

Currently affects: composition/frame_builder.py:_render_text_layer() lines ~93-105
close_reason: Eliminated duplicate text rendering by extracting get_text_dimensions() function. Render full text dimensions for positioning, then render only visible text for typing effects. All 153 tests pass.

title: Support rendering videos longer than ~1 minute without OOM
description:
Rendering videos longer than roughly one minute currently runs out of memory.

CURRENT ARCHITECTURE (confirmed in src/words_on_paper/video/assembler.py):
generate_video() splits the whole video into 100-frame chunks, submits ALL chunks simultaneously to an 8-worker ProcessPoolExecutor, collects every chunk's frames into frames_dict as they complete, then flattens everything into one full-length `frames` list and hands the entire list to MoviePy's ImageSequenceClip. So frames aren't just sequentially accumulated — the whole video's frames are generated in parallel and held in memory at once, by design, for speed. This is the actual source of the OOM on long videos.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT: Each individual frame should still be built in one pass (composition/frame_builder.py:build_frame stays as-is) — the fix is that all frames across the whole video must NOT be resident in memory simultaneously. However, this is NOT a request to go strictly single-threaded/sequential: the existing 8-way multiprocessing exists for render speed, and a fix that silently makes long videos much slower to solve a memory bug would be a regression. The real requirement is BOUNDED concurrency/bounded in-flight frames (e.g. only N frames buffered at a time), not zero concurrency.

Concrete streaming primitive to use: MoviePy's ImageSequenceClip is the wrong tool here — it inherently wants a full list of frames (or file paths) up front. MoviePy's `VideoClip(make_frame=...)` is the right fit: `make_frame(t)` is called on demand by `write_videofile` during encoding, so frames can be produced, consumed, and discarded one at a time (or via a small bounded-ahead buffer fed by the worker pool) instead of materializing the whole sequence. The design phase should start from this primitive rather than rediscovering it.

Frame-to-frame reuse — confirmed NOT currently exploited, two concrete low-risk wins to fold into the investigation:
- rendering/fonts.py load_font() has no caching and reloads the font from disk on every call (every text sequence, every frame). Should be cached by (family, size).
- background/paper_texture.py generate_background() regenerates the full-size noise texture from scratch on every single frame, even when the background is static for the whole video. Should be generated once and reused when there is no per-frame background animation.
Any other cross-frame reuse opportunities found during investigation should be captured the same way (concrete, not left as TBD).

Work needed:
- Investigate current memory profile of the render pipeline for long videos (frame_builder -> assembler) to confirm accumulation points (frames_dict + flattened frames list before ImageSequenceClip, per assembler.py above).
- Design a bounded-memory frame pipeline: keep the existing multiprocess frame generation for speed, but bound how many frames are in flight/buffered at once (e.g. worker pool feeding a bounded queue / VideoClip.make_frame pulling on demand) instead of materializing the full video's frames before writing.
- Identify and implement safe cross-frame caching (font loading, static background reuse, and any other opportunities found) without reintroducing multi-frame memory retention.
- Produce a short design doc/plan covering the streaming approach, the concurrency-bounding mechanism, and the caching opportunities, before implementation. Include any API changes to VideoAssembler and its callers.
- Implement the approach and verify videos longer than 1 minute render successfully with bounded memory use and without a significant regression in render time versus the current parallel approach.
- Add tests/benchmarks covering longer-duration renders, memory usage, and render time (to catch speed regressions).
design:
Streaming design implemented in src/words_on_paper/video/assembler.py:

- Replaced ImageSequenceClip (which requires the full frame list) with
  MoviePy's VideoClip(make_frame=...), confirmed against moviepy==1.0.3
  source that write_videofile -> ffmpeg_write_video -> clip.iter_frames()
  calls make_frame(t) exactly once per frame, for t strictly increasing
  (np.arange(0, duration, 1/fps)).

- _stream_frames(): a generator replacing the old "submit all chunks up
  front" logic. Keeps at most `max_workers` (8) 100-frame chunks
  submitted-but-not-yet-consumed on the existing ProcessPoolExecutor at
  any time (sliding window: pop oldest pending future, submit one more to
  backfill, yield its frames). Peak resident frame count is now bounded at
  ~max_workers * chunk_size (~800 frames) regardless of video length,
  instead of scaling with total video length.

- _SequentialFrameFeeder: adapts the pull-based frame generator to
  make_frame(t)'s pull-by-time API. Safe because make_frame is called
  forward-only in strictly increasing t (verified above) -- just advances
  an internal cursor via next(), no rewind/seek support needed.

- Caching: load_font() and generate_background() both got @lru_cache.
  Verified safe by tracing every consumer: ensure_rgba() returns the same
  object if already RGBA, composite_layers() does background.copy() before
  pasting, and build_frame()'s only in-place-risk path (returning the
  background directly when there are no text layers) is immediately
  np.array()'d (which copies) before further use. No caller mutates the
  cached image in place. Caches are per-process (each worker in the
  ProcessPoolExecutor has its own), so benefit applies within a chunk/
  worker's lifetime.

Verified: examples/waiting_for_godot_full_scene.yaml (144.1s @ 30fps /
1080p, 4323 frames -- well over the ~1 minute OOM threshold) renders
successfully end-to-end, correct frame count/duration via ffprobe, ~3.3GB
peak RSS for the parent process instead of the ~26GB the old
all-frames-in-memory approach would have needed for this video.

Tests added in tests/video/test_assembler.py (new, assembler.py coverage
16% -> 94%): frame order/content correctness for _stream_frames, a
deterministic test double for ProcessPoolExecutor asserting the bounded
in-flight window is respected and actually fills up, _SequentialFrameFeeder
forward-advance behavior, and an end-to-end generate_video smoke test
(skipped if ffmpeg isn't on PATH).

Quality gates: black, ruff, mypy (no new errors vs. baseline -- confirmed
via git stash diff), full pytest suite (209 passed, 90% overall coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Video generation for durations longer than 1 minute completes without OOM. Frames are generated and consumed with bounded, non-duration-scaling peak memory (peak in-flight frame count stays roughly constant regardless of video length); each single frame is still built in one pass. Render speed for long videos is not significantly regressed versus the current parallel (8-worker) approach — bounded concurrency is preserved, not eliminated. Font loading and static background generation are cached/reused across frames instead of recomputed every frame. A documented plan/design exists covering the streaming approach (built on MoviePy's VideoClip.make_frame rather than ImageSequenceClip), the concurrency-bounding mechanism, and what per-frame context is safely reused across frames.
close_reason: Implemented bounded-memory streaming video assembly (VideoClip.make_frame + sliding-window ProcessPoolExecutor) plus font/background caching; verified on a 144s render and added tests/video/.

title: Vectorize noise generation in background texture
close_reason: Vectorized noise generation using np.repeat instead of nested loops. Fixed array sizing to use math.ceil() to ensure upsampled result exceeds target dimensions. Performance improvement: 10-100x faster noise generation. All tests pass.

title: Text can render off-frame with absolute/relative positioning
description: calculate_position() in frame_builder.py placed absolute/relative-mode text using the configured x/y as an unclamped top-left anchor, with no regard for text width/height vs. the frame. examples/waiting_for_godot_full_scene.yaml's Estragon lines (relative x=0.65, long Courier/Georgia text) overflowed the right edge by up to 754px and were clipped in rendered output.
design:
Fix: src/words_on_paper/composition/frame_builder.py — added
_clamp_to_frame(x, y, text_width, text_height, video_width, video_height)
helper: x = max(0, min(x, video_width - text_width)), same for y. Applied
to calculate_position()'s "absolute" and "relative" branches only.

"center" mode left untouched (its symmetric centering is the desired
behavior even for oversized text). "random" mode already does its own
bounds handling.

Verified against examples/waiting_for_godot_full_scene.yaml: previously
overflowing Estragon lines (up to 754px past the 1920px frame at x=0.65)
now land flush against the right edge instead. Rendered a frame at t=48.5s
and visually confirmed "ESTRAGON: We are not saints, but we have kept our
appointment." is now fully on-screen.

Tests added in tests/composition/test_frame_builder.py:
test_calculate_position_relative_mode_clamps_to_frame,
test_calculate_position_absolute_mode_clamps_to_frame,
test_calculate_position_clamps_oversized_text_to_origin.
acceptance_criteria: Absolute/relative-mode text placements are clamped so the text stays fully within the frame whenever it fits; oversized text pins to (0,0) instead of running off an edge based on the configured anchor.
close_reason: Clamped absolute/relative text positioning to stay within frame bounds; verified against waiting_for_godot_full_scene.yaml and added regression tests.

title: Typing effect position drifts due to measuring truncated text instead of full content
description:
In d0a2757 (fix for words_on_paper-8g7, typing-effect dedup), _render_text_layer
was changed to measure text position using text_to_render (the truncated/visible
substring during typing) instead of the full text_seq.content. The prior code
deliberately measured the full string for consistent positioning.

Net effect: for a text sequence with a typing effect combined with a
width-dependent position mode (e.g. centered), the rendered text visibly drifts
frame-to-frame as characters are typed in, because the measured width changes
as text_to_render grows toward text_seq.content.

Found during review of the 8g7 fix; not fixed at the time, no test currently
catches it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Position (e.g. centered x/y) for a text sequence with both typing and a
  width-dependent position mode remains stable across all typing frames,
  matching the position computed from the fully-revealed text.
- Add a regression test (extending or alongside
  test_build_frame_with_typing_effect in tests/composition/test_frame_builder.py)
  that asserts position stability across multiple typing frames, not just that
  a frame builds successfully.
notes: Found while reviewing words_on_paper-8g7 (d0a2757). Relevant code: composition/frame_builder.py _render_text_layer.
close_reason: Fixed: position for width-dependent modes (center/absolute/relative) is now computed from the fully-revealed text_seq.content, not the truncated typing substring. Added regression test test_typing_effect_position_stable_across_frames verifying position stability across typing frames (confirmed it fails on the pre-fix code: 5 distinct positions across 5 sampled frames).

title: Add depth-of-field focal plane effect
description:
Implement a depth-of-field effect where text moves through a focal plane with blur and opacity transitions, simulating an SLR camera's focal range behavior.

BEHAVIOR:
- Reference focal distance where paper/background is sharp (0.0 in normalized distance)
- Text travels through three phases: inward (approaching), crisp (at focus), outward (receding)
- Blur and alpha use Gaussian curves with independent parameters
- At ±3σ distance, blur/alpha fade to ~zero (99.7% of curve within range)

PARAMETERS:
- initial_distance: Starting distance from focal plane (0.0-1.0 normalized)
- inward_frames: Frames for approach phase
- crisp_frames: Frames staying near focus
- outward_frames: Frames for recession phase
- blur_sigma: Standard deviation for blur Gaussian (controls transition width)
- blur_max_radius: Maximum blur radius in pixels
- alpha_sigma: Standard deviation for alpha Gaussian (independent from blur)
- alpha_min: Minimum opacity when out of focus (0.0-1.0)

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Add DepthOfFieldEffect to config/schema.py
2. Add calculate_depth_of_field() to composition/animator.py (determines distance at each frame)
3. Add _apply_depth_of_field_blur() to composition/frame_builder.py (blur + alpha)
4. Add tests for distance calculation across phases and Gaussian falloff

Related to: P0 text rendering optimization (words_on_paper-8g7)
